How much does it cost to run a fish tank?

A typical fish tank uses about 100 watts (30–300W depending on the model). Used for 24 hours per day, 7 days a week, it costs about 32p per day and £115 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per day
32p
About £115 a year at 24 hours per day, 7 days a week.

Standing charge not included.

About these figures

Worth knowing: Heater cycles; lights on part of day.

Source for the typical figure: Typical range (estimate). See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Check the power rating on the plug or label for the most accurate figure.
  • A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what a device uses.
  • Turn things off at the wall when not in use.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a fish tank per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 100W model costs about 1.3p an hour, allowing for it running at full power about 50% of the time.

How much does it cost to run a fish tank per year?

About £115 a year, based on 24 hours per day, 7 days a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my fish tank's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
